title: Output Rendering & UI Layer
scope: Catalog the UX niceties: terminal formatting, colors, progress indicators, interactive prompts, markdown/code rendering.

terminal.primary_rendering: rich 14.2.0 (Console, Live, Panel, Table, Progress, Syntax, Markdown, Columns, Group, Text)
terminal.cli_framework: typer 0.21.1 (command dispatch; typer.echo for simple text, plain mode output)
terminal_notes: prompt_toolkit is used for interactive prompts/completions and full-screen TUI forms (Application objects with Container layout).
rich is the workhorse for all structured console output: panels, tables, live streaming views, code syntax highlighting, markdown, spinners, progress bars.
A custom prompt_toolkit Application is used for full-screen modal overlays (approval/question prompts) via _BtwModalDelegate.

A dedicated background keyboard-thread listener (_KeyboardListener in interactive_input.py) bypasses prompt_toolkit for global hotkeys during streaming (arrows, digits 1-6, ctrl-e, escape, space, enter).
kimi-cli is embedded as a web worker subprocess in --wire stdio mode (see runner/process.py KimiCLIRunner); the web UI is a React frontend that consumes the JSON-RPC 2.0 WebSocket feed.

web.markdown: streamdown (streaming markdown with remark-gfm, rehype-katex, rehype-highlight via shiki)
web.syntax_highlighting: shiki (lazy dynamic import; one-light / one-dark-pro themes; HighlightCache avoids async reflow; line-number ShikiTransformer)
web.math: katex (rendered inline and block via rehype-katex in streamdown)
web.styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (oklch design tokens, custom dark variant @custom-variant dark, shadcn/ui patterns)
web.ui_primitives: radix-ui (@radix-ui/react-dialog, tooltip, tabs, progress, scroll-area, dropdown-menu, select)
web.layout: CSS flexbox/grid with responsive breakpoints; sidepanel (threads, mcp, hooks), main chat area, bottom input composer
web.state: React hooks (useState/useLayoutEffect/useEffect), ResizeObserver for overflow detection, useRef for scroll anchoring

toad_tui.availability: Python 3.14+ only (kimi term subcommand); optional dependency
toad_tui.architecture: Full-screen Textual TUI that connects to kimi-cli via the ACP server subprocess (kimi acp), not used in standard shell mode

Ctrl-O to open response in external $EDITOR (editor picker via typer)
Bracketed-paste support, bracketed undo history, multiline undo
Vi/emacs editing mode with config toggle

interactive_menus.uses: RadioList, formatted with rich rendering, modal overlay via _BtwModalDelegate
Application with Container layout, Arrow/home/end navigation, Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel
Single-choice prompt with y/n, arrow keys, rendered with Rich Panel header
_BtwModalDelegate replacing the prompt line with a modal dialog body

approval_prompt.renderer: prompt_toolkit Application embedded as a modal overlay, body rendered with rich Panel + Markdown

question_prompt.renderer: prompt_toolkit Application modal overlay with Rich Panel, scrollable option list, type-to-filter

slash_command_mode.completer: SlashCommandCompleter (fuzzy, grouped; BulletColumns for help display)

non_interactive_modes.notes: Bypasses all rich formatting; outputs raw committed text or structured JSONL via the WireMessageEnvelope

keyboard_listener.purpose: Dedicated background thread reading raw terminal input; handles global hotkeys that must work during rich Live rendering (prompt_toolkit is paused during streaming)

pattern: Incremental ContentBlock accumulates markdown text; markdown-it parser detects complete block boundaries;
Confirmed blocks are flushed to console.print() (committed to scrollback);
Uncommitted 'tail' remains in a transient rich Live area for cursor-like live update;
Block type dispatch (TextPart, ToolCallPart, ToolResult, etc.) via content-block-type -> renderer mapping;
Rich Live context running a manual refresh loop (spinner animation ~0.08s interval);
live.stop() before pager/synchronous console.print(); live.start() after to avoid flicker;
compose() returns a Group/Align/Padding rendered into the Live canvas;

commit_and_scroll.pattern: Committed output written via console.print(); on newline overflow, Console's built-in pager (_KimiPager) or auto-scroll keeps the viewport at the latest committed content.
commit_and_scroll.pager: src/kimi_cli/ui/shell/console.py (_KimiPager) - subclasses rich.pager.Pager, forces MANPAGER unset and uses the default system pager only when --pager flag is set

panel_table_layout.diff_rendering: src/kimi_cli/utils/rich/diff_render.py (DiffRender) - produces rich Table/Panel with line numbers, color-coded +/- via theme-aware DiffColors, git-style unified diff

custom_markdown.impl: Custom Markdown class subclassing rich.markdown.Markdown with a forked markdown-it parser; adds strikethrough and table extensions; renders via custom CodeBlock/Syntax highlighting; NEUTRAL_MARKDOWN_THEME applied; render_to_ansi() bridges to prompt_toolkit via render() with ANSI stripping

syntax_highlighting.impl: Subclass of rich.syntax.Syntax; loads a custom KIMI_ANSI_THEME (Pygments Style) via a custom Theme; line_numbers toggle; background_color and word_wrap config; used in all code block rendering

bullet_columns.impl: Custom Columns subclass that renders a leading bullet (•) before each rendered item, used for help/option listings and slash command hints

spinner_progress.spinner: rich.spinner.Spinner ('dots', 'moon', etc.) animated at ~12fps alongside Live refresh
spinner_progress.status: console.status() with custom Spinner + bottom_toolbar for MCP connection status
spinner_progress.progress_bar: src/kimi_cli/ui/shell/usage.py (rich.progress.ProgressBar wrapper showing token usage with label, total, completed, and spinner)

web_streaming_render.impl: streamdown component consumes streaming JSON tokens; renders markdown; applies remark-gfm, rehype-katex, shiki highlighting; maintains message list in react-virtuoso Virtuoso

web_code_block.impl: Async shiki highlighter with lazy dynamic import; caches highlight results to avoid reflow (ResizeObserver/measure); dual theme (one-light/one-dark-pro via CSS var toggle); collapsible overflow (COLLAPSE_THRESHOLD=300 lines); line numbers via ShikiTransformer; copy-to-clipboard button

web_virtualization.impl: react-virtuoso Virtuoso with sticky footer at bottom; messages keyed by wire message id; auto-scroll on new content; scroll-lock detection for history browse

two built-in schemes: 'dark' and 'light', selected via --theme flag / THEME env var;
theme-aware color constants exported: DiffColors, ToolbarColors, MCPPromptColors, TaskBrowserStyle, QuestionStyle, ApprovalStyle, SlashCompletionsStyle;

terminal_markdown_theme.impl: rich.theme.Theme mapping markdown element names (e.g. 'markdown.h1', 'markdown.code', 'markdown.code_block') to style strings; neutral colors that work on both dark and light terminal backgrounds;

syntax_theme.impl: Custom Pygments-based Style for KimiSyntax; token-level color mapping for language constructs (keywords, strings, comments, operators);

OKLCH design-token CSS variables (--background, --foreground, --card, --primary, etc.) with @theme inline mapping to Tailwind;
Custom dark variant: @custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *)); theme toggled via <html class='dark'>;

special.detail: prompt_toolkit Application objects with full-screen Container layouts (not just input widgets); used for task browsing (RadioList), session picking, and the interactive setup wizard; rendered modally via _BtwModalDelegate which overlays the entire prompt line
Raw stdin fd read in a dedicated thread so hotkeys work even when the rich Live display owns the terminal; bypasses prompt_toolkit entirely during agent streaming turns

_wrap_osc8_as_zero_width wraps OSC 8 hyperlink escape sequences as prompt_toolkit ZeroWidthEscape so terminal emulators that support it can render clickable links without breaking rich/prompt_toolkit layout calculations
Detects terminal cursor column position (Unix via ANSI device-status-report / Windows fallback) to insert line breaks that align subsequent text under the current prompt column
Subclasses rich.pager.Pager; strips MANPAGER env var in the pager subprocess to prevent garbled output from nested pagers; only activates on explicit --pager flag

@router.websocket('/{session_id}/stream') endpoint authenticates by session token + LAN-only check, then pipes JSON-RPC 2.0 messages (type + payload via WireMessageEnvelope) to the browser; KimiCLIRunner runs kimi-cli in --wire stdio mode in a subprocess, parses stdout JSON-RPC, and broadcasts via the WebSocket; supports replay from wire.jsonl

Wire protocol uses Pydantic-v2 BaseModel discriminated unions: type Event = TurnBegin | SteerInput | ... | BtwEnd (19 variants); type Request = ApprovalRequest | ToolCallRequest | QuestionRequest | HookRequest; type WireMessage = Event | Request. A WireRequestEnvelope wraps the typed payload with a string 'type' discriminator + 'payload' dict; serialize via msg.model_dump(mode='json'), deserialize via WireMessageEnvelope.model_validate({...}) then envelope.to_wire_message(). TypeAliasType unions are reflected at runtime via flatten_union() (resolves PEP 604 / Union / TypeAliasType into a flat tuple of classes) so isinstance() dispatch + TypeAdapter validation works without manual discriminator fields on every variant. Literal-typed action fields (e.g. ApprovalResponse.type.Kind = Literal['approve','approve_for_session','reject']) act as a second-level discriminator inside request/response payloads.

proposal: The most reusable Pydantic-v2 UX pattern in kimi-cli is its wire message envelope: define every interaction as a flat BaseModel, compose them into discriminated-union type aliases (type X = A | B | C), then serialize to {type: ClassName, payload: model_dump(mode='json')} for the transport layer and round-trip with model_validate() + TypeAdapter. The flatten_union() helper bridges PEP 604 unions to runtime isinstance() dispatch — so a single message handler can receive one envelope, validate its type discriminator, and downcast via the right variant with full Pydantic validation on the payload. For ai-factory, adopt this same envelope pattern for the agent-to-conductor / agent-to-agent control signals (StepBegin, StepInterrupted, ApprovalRequest, QuestionRequest) so UI renderers (TUI or web) can consume a uniform JSON-RPC-like stream without the renderer knowing the upstream agent framework. This mirrors KC-02's discovery that kimi-cli emits rich interactive prompts (ApprovalResponse, QuestionRequest) over a typed union — the same union can drive ai-factory's own interactive approval gates by swapping the renderer (prompt_toolkit modal vs Web modal) while keeping the Pydantic contract identical.

pydantic_ai_2_impl.pattern: Discriminated-union control envelopes via TypeAdapter output_type
pydantic_ai_2_impl.code:
from pydantic import BaseModel, TypeAdapter
from pydantic_ai import Agent
class TurnBegin(BaseModel): type: Literal['turn_begin']
class ToolCallRequest(BaseModel): type: Literal['tool_call']; call_id: str
class ApprovalRequest(BaseModel): type: Literal['approval']; ask: str
Env = TypeAdapter[Union[TurnBegin, ToolCallRequest, ApprovalRequest]]
render = Agent('anthropic:claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022', output_type=Env)
env = render.run_sync('emit next control signal').output  # Pydantic-validated envelope
pydantic_ai_2_impl.why_now: ai-factory's conductor must ingest typed control signals from renderers without trusting free-form LLM prose; pydantic-ai 2.0 validates the discriminated union at the agent boundary via output_type=TypeAdapter, enforcing kimi-cli's wire envelope contract inside the structured run_sync output.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.harness_gap: LLMs keep failing free-form control-signal emission (hallucinated type names, missing payload keys, stray prose). A Pydantic-validated envelope rejects malformed outputs at run_sync instead of silently corrupting the TUI/web render stream - Fail Loudly, Fail Cheaply.
